correctness.rationale: From arXiv:2408.07646 Theorem 1.1 and combinatorial Alexander duality, only H5 is nonzero, of rank N. For each involution, the proof independently classifies all 2-orbit/1-orbit face unions of at most six vertices using the bipartite matching criterion. The resulting exact signed reduced Lefschetz sums are -N,-f,+f, with identity N. Character orthogonality for C2xC2 and rational transfer give the claimed module and quotient ranks. A standalone verifier checks 99 nontrivial traces n=4..36 and full F2 boundary complexes n=4..8; all passed. Infinite-family validity rests on the explicit count, not these finite tests.

originality.rationale: The same-object primary theorem (arXiv:2408.07646) supplies only ordinary total-cut sphere counts; its proof gives no symmetry maps. The 2026 robust-clique primary also treats nonequivariant homotopy and general definitions. The closest indexed equivariant ladder result concerns robustness three, whose second-square representation cannot imply the degree-five, square-triple character for robustness four. Targeted semantic and external literature searches found no dominating same-parameter result; limited access to certain indexed public full texts remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Two highly relevant published published-finding corpus records at k=3 could be compared only through mathematical summaries, since linked full-text pages were inaccessible. Their different robustness parameter is a specific noncoverage reason.
An unindexed general equivariant Alexander-dual reduction may encode the same formula, despite no direct match found.
The public records are not an exhaustive census of every manuscript or unpublished derivation.

value.rationale: This gives the complete degree-five V4 character for all widths of a canonical ladder family at robustness four, refining the known binomial sphere rank and distinguishing reflection quotients with a nontrivial parity-sensitive central-square contribution. The full quotient is rationally acyclic despite large rank upstairs. These are natural topological group actions and quotient invariants, not arbitrary numerical slices.
